etymology: Latin: argumentum ex silentio - nothing was said, so the nothing is read as a statement.
committed_when: A record is missing and a conclusion is convenient.
tell: The argument rests on what nobody wrote down.
counter: Ask whether anyone would have written it down. If the answer is no, the silence is not evidence of anything.
senses: Concluding something from the absence of a record, when the record would not have mentioned it either way.
It works because silence is genuinely informative sometimes. Whether it is depends entirely on whether the silence was supposed to be broken, and that question is the one the sentence skips.
example: *“No complaints were filed, so everyone was satisfied.”* Nobody knew there was a form.

confused_with.tell: Ignorance is about missing evidence in general; silence is about a specific record that was never kept.
